extraction_scope: Worker-6 source-reviewed mechanism ontology; mechanism claims are bounded to directly supported membrane disruption, leakage, folding/stability, and cytotoxicity context.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: The paper evaluates ln65 diastereomers as membrane-disruptive alpha-helical antimicrobial peptides; MIC, hemolysis, and EYPG/EYPC vesicle leakage data support membrane-interaction/leakage context but do not justify a narrower molecular target claim.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: ln65/dln65/ln69/dln69, HP1-HP37, 2ln65, 2ln69, and related source-table peptides
mechanism_claims.limitations: Membrane-disruptive context is supported; no receptor/enzyme target or exact kill-pathway mechanism is inferred.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Lowercase D-residue diastereomer notation is source-preserved; CD and X-ray crystallography are used to relate stereochemistry and alpha-helicity to antibacterial activity, hemolysis, and toxicity trends.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: mixed-chirality ln65 derivatives with Table 3 crystallography examples FHP5/FHP8/FHP30/FHP31
mechanism_claims.limitations: Structure-property evidence supports curation context and caution framing, not a standalone direct antimicrobial mechanism class.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Serum stability and mammalian cytotoxicity are evaluated as property-optimization outcomes for selected diastereomers, including HEK293 and A549 cell assays.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: selected diastereomers with serum stability and cytotoxicity data
mechanism_claims.limitations: Toxicity and stability are curated as activity/toxicity/property evidence, not as antimicrobial mode-of-action claims.
